report:
A, B, and C confirmed a working plan, not a sale. No discount, price, payment plan, or purchase has been approved. C has not agreed to sign off on a discounted sale, and B cannot accept a discount without clear terms and shares.

The shared list records each sister's needs, concerns, and expectations, plus my own concerns about a fair process, equal access to facts, and the risk of a private side deal. I checked my concerns with all three, weighed drafts against the list, and stated my disagreement with any discount that would lower B's or C's share. All three confirmed that I recorded their views accurately.

The working plan calls for a joint search for the will and estate papers, shared copies, legal guidance from a lawyer or the local court that handles wills, an independent appraisal, a shared list of estate costs, and shares set by the will and estate process. Full market value is only a comparison number after valuation. If A and her husband cannot buy at that price, the group can compare an open-market sale. Any discount would require free written agreement from all three, with A and her husband paying the difference from their own funds. No one should sign or pay until the facts, review time, and written estate agreement are in place.

No sister has a lawyer or court contact, and no date or time has been set for the joint search. A and C offered to help coordinate, and B can join once a date and time are agreed. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. A lawyer and the person handling the estate may need to act.
